tracks.title: I Only Know Your Eyes
tracks.subject: Two day-shift packers on a biscuit factory's custard-cream line fall in love knowing only each other's eyes between hairnet and blue beard snood, and outside the gate she walks straight past him until he cups his hands over his beard.
tracks.caption: Uplifting vocal trance, 2020s anthemic trance with a long breakdown and snare-roll build. Detuned supersaw lead in wide sidechained chord stabs, rolling offbeat sub-bass, gated pluck arpeggio in sixteenth notes, four-on-the-floor 909 kick with offbeat open hi-hats, bright piano chords in the breakdown. Wide club mix, clean polished master. Female soprano, strong bright full-voice topline with long open notes on the hook. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 138 BPM, A minor. Euphoric, yearning, bright. No rap, no autotune effect, no trap hi-hats, no distorted guitars, no whispered vocals.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - pluck arpeggio, soft kick, filtered supersaw]

[Verse 1]
Six a.m. on the custard-cream line
Hairnet, blue snood, gloves on tight
All I know of you is your eyes
Over the biscuits going by

[Pre-Chorus]
Every shift you pass me the tray
Every shift I forget what to say

[Chorus]
I only know your eyes, your eyes
Over the belt in the factory light
I only know your eyes, your eyes
Tell me it's you, tell me it's right

[Verse 2]
Out at the gate I walked on by
A stranger's chin, a stranger's smile
Then you cupped your hands over your beard
And there were the eyes, so near

[Pre-Chorus]
Every shift you pass me the tray
Now I know just what to say

[Chorus]
I know your face now, I know your eyes
Out in the open, out in the light
I know your face now, I know your eyes
Take off the snood, you're mine tonight

[Outro - arpeggio alone, kick drops out]
I only know your eyes

tracks.title: Eleven Elections
tracks.subject: Two poll clerks share a trestle table in a village hall only on election days, eleven in twenty years, until she catches herself hoping for a snap election and, as the box is sealed at ten, he asks why wait for the next.
tracks.caption: Salsa, classic New York salsa dura style with a live orchestra feel. Piano playing a syncopated montuno in octaves, two trumpets and two trombones on punchy unison riffs and mambo breaks, baby bass on a rolling tumbao, congas with timbales and cowbell locked to a 2-3 clave, güiro scraping eighth notes. Live room recording, warm analog horns. Female mezzo-soprano, bright full chest voice, three-voice coro answering the refrain. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 92 BPM, E-flat major. Warm, hopeful, wry. No electronic beats, no reggaeton dembow, no autotune, no rap, no synth pads, no distorted guitars.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - piano montuno, congas, horn hit]

[Verse 1]
Trestle table in the village hall
Pencils on strings and a flask of tea
Eleven elections in twenty years
You across the table from me

[Pre-Chorus]
I read the news and I caught myself
Hoping they'd call another one

[Chorus]
Eleven elections, I counted every one
Eleven elections, and the polls are almost done
Why wait, why wait, why wait for the next
Why wait for the next one, come on

[Verse 2]
Ten o'clock, we seal the box
You turn the key and you clear your throat
You say it quiet, over the wax
And you pass me a pencil with a note

[Pre-Chorus]
I read it twice and I read it slow
It says, why wait for another one

[Chorus]
Eleven elections, and I'll keep this one
Eleven elections, and the counting's done
Why wait, why wait, no, don't wait for the next
Dance with me now, come on

[Outro - mambo horns, congas, piano]
Why wait, why wait for the next

tracks.title: Run, Hank, Run
tracks.subject: A wife on the Ocmulgee riverbank in Macon watches a gust lift her husband's auburn toupee off his head and a neighbour's coonhound trot off with it, and has to decide whether to admit she has known since the wedding day.
tracks.caption: Southern rock, 1970s-style Georgia boogie with harmonised twin-lead riffs. Two overdriven Les Paul guitars on twin leads, one switching to bottleneck slide in open E to answer the voice, Hammond B3 organ through a rotating Leslie speaker, rolling honky-tonk piano fills, live drums on a loose straight-eighth boogie with heavy backbeat. Live-room recording, warm tape saturation. Female alto, strong gritty chest voice, each line answered by the slide. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 96 BPM, E major. Wry, smoky, defiant. No rap, no drum machine, no autotune, no synth pads, no trap hi-hats, no polished pop production.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - bottleneck slide, Hammond swell, drums]

[Verse 1]
Hank's on the Ocmulgee with a rod in his hand
Auburn hair thick as the day we wed
The wind comes up off the water at noon
And lifts it clean off the top of his head

[Pre-Chorus]
That coonhound's trotting, that coonhound's running
Off down the bank with a mouthful of Hank

[Chorus]
Run, Hank, run, that hound's got your hair
Thirty years I've pretended not to know
I saw the glue on our wedding day
Honey, let the dog go

[Verse 2]
You're standing there pink as a ham in the sun
Both hands on a head you never showed me
I hand you my cap and you don't say a word
Hound's in the kudzu, and so is the story

[Pre-Chorus]
I say, Hank, I've known since ninety-four
And I'd have married you bald as an egg

[Chorus]
Stay, Hank, stay, let the hound keep your hair
Thirty years I've pretended not to know
I loved the man under the glue
Honey, now I let it show

[Outro - slide guitar, Hammond fades]
Let the dog go

tracks.title: I Only Asked About the Fountain
tracks.subject: A man new to town goes to his first residents' association AGM only to ask why the square's fountain has been dry since 2016, raises his hand at the wrong moment, and walks home elected treasurer, carrying a biscuit tin with £41.17 in it.
tracks.caption: Vintage calypso, 1950s Trinidadian storytelling calypso with a gentle shuffle. Nylon-string acoustic guitar strumming a syncopated calypso rhythm, upright bass on a bouncing two-beat, clarinet answering each vocal line, muted trumpet riffs between verses, bongos and shak-shak maracas. Dry vintage studio sound, close mics, slight tape warmth. Male tenor, lilting storytelling melody with crisp diction, chorus singers answering the refrain. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 108 BPM, F major. Witty, sunny, mock-indignant. No electronic drums, no soca synths, no autotune, no rap, no electric guitar distortion, no modern pop production.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - nylon guitar, clarinet, bongos]

[Verse 1]
I moved to the street in the month of May
Went to the meeting to have my say
One little question, I thought it was fair
Why is the fountain dry in the square?

[Pre-Chorus]
The chairman said, any volunteer?
I raised my hand to scratch my ear

[Chorus]
I only asked about the fountain
Now I'm the treasurer, Lord have mercy
Forty-one pounds and seventeen pence
In a biscuit tin, I only asked about the fountain

[Verse 2]
They gave me the tin and they gave me the key
A ledger, a pencil and a cup of tea
Dry since twenty-sixteen, they say
And my forty-one pounds won't fix it today

[Pre-Chorus]
The chairman said, all in favour, aye
I said, I only came to ask why

[Chorus]
I only asked about the fountain
Now I'm the treasurer, who will help me
Forty-one pounds and seventeen pence
And a dry fountain, I only asked about the fountain

[Outro - clarinet, muted trumpet, shak-shak]
Only asked about the fountain

tracks.title: Nana's Got an Anchor
tracks.subject: A grandmother who has never been to sea gets an anchor tattooed on her forearm for her seventieth birthday and hides it under cardigans all summer from her disapproving daughter, who finally rolls up her own sleeve to show a swallow hidden since 1996.
tracks.caption: Sea shanty, traditional British call-and-response work shanty with a rowdy pub-session feel. Crew chorus with foot stomps and hand claps on the beat, anglo concertina pumping chords, fiddle doubling the tune with droning double-stops, bodhran hand drum on a steady thump. Live pub-room recording, stomps and claps close to the mics. Male baritone shantyman, strong open chest voice, every line answered by a mixed crew chorus in unison. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 100 BPM, D minor. Rowdy, fond, cheeky. No drum kit, no electric guitar, no synths, no autotune, no rap, no pop production.
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro - concertina, stomps, bodhran]

[Verse 1]
Nana turned seventy in the month of May
Never been to sea, not a single day
Walked in a tattoo parlour on the quay
Said, an anchor on my forearm, lad, for me

[Pre-Chorus]
Heave away, heave away
Never been to sea, heave away

[Chorus]
Oh, Nana's got an anchor, heave away, haul away
Hid beneath her cardigan all through the day
Nana's got an anchor and she's not going to say
Heave away, my Nana, heave away

[Verse 2]
Her daughter says, Mother, it's thirty degrees
Why the cardigan, why the sleeves
Then the daughter rolls her own sleeve high
There's a swallow from ninety-six, oh my

Heave away, heave away

[Chorus]
Oh, Nana's got an anchor, and the daughter's got a bird
Hid beneath the cardigans, and neither said a word
Two of them have inked their arms, and both are rather proud
Heave away, my Nana, sing it loud

[Outro - concertina, fiddle, stomps]
Heave away, my Nana, heave away

tracks.subject: Chị Thoa has guarded the steel stationery cabinet on the third floor of a Quy Nhơn trading company for twenty years like a general holding a mountain pass: one ballpoint each, only against the dead one and a signature, director included; the morning her own pen dies mid-form she has to borrow one from the junior clerk she turned away an hour earlier, and he makes her sign for it.
tracks.caption: Hát bội crossover pop, mock-heroic tuồng stage style over a modern backbeat. Ornamented kèn bầu shawm fanfare riffs, booming trống chiến war drum rolls and rim clacks, đồng la gong with chập chõa cymbal crashes at phrase ends, sliding đàn cò fiddle countermelody, pop drum kit with sub bass on a steady four-on-the-floor backbeat. Punchy theatrical stage-pop mix, bright and dry. Female bright mezzo-soprano, projected full voice, clearly sung melody with short hát bội slides at phrase ends. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 108 BPM, D minor. Mischievous, mock-heroic swagger. No rapping, no chanting, no autotune, no trap hi-hats, no EDM drops, no electric guitar.

tracks.mood: tender, warm, quietly proud, gently buoyant
tracks.subject: Best friends since first grade, one 191 cm and always back-row centre, one 158 cm and always front-row centre in every class photo, open a café together; for the opening-day picture the short one stands on a milk crate so their heads are level.
tracks.caption: Mandarin sunshine pop, baroque-pop arrangement in a steady 4/4 with stacked close harmonies. Glockenspiel doubling the chorus tune, harpsichord playing bright broken chords, pizzicato strings with a sustained string pad under the chorus, French horn countermelody, round melodic electric bass, light kit with tambourine on the backbeat. Bright analog studio recording, warm tape glow, wide layered harmonies. Male tenor lead, warm and full-voiced, with stacked close-harmony backing vocals on the chorus. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 100 BPM, E-flat major. Tender, warm, quietly proud mood. No rap, no autotune, no electronic drums, no distorted guitars, no synth bass, no acoustic strumming.
